page: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is a virtualized server instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. Built on the ARMv8 architecture using Cortex-A72 cores, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It does not feature local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data indicates that the first-generation Graviton processor delivers modest performance compared to modern x86 or newer ARM architectures. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieves average single-core and multi-core CPU performance. However, memory subsystem performance is constrained, with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 12.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 6.77 GB/sec, both falling into the lower performance tier. General computing benchmarks, such as Geekbench and PassMark, also place this instance in the lower percentiles, reflecting its legacy hardware profile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the a1.xlarge offers an entry-level entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, making it suitable for testing and porting applications to the arm64 architecture. However, the performance tradeoffs are significant, particularly in memory-intensive tasks and database operations, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 1263.44 and a Redis SET throughput of 2.13 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for lightweight, scale-out workloads such as basic web serving, development environments, and simple containerized microservices that do not require high memory bandwidth or advanced vector instructions.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is an entry-level ARM-based instance powered by first-generation AWS Graviton Cortex-A72 processors. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores, 1 thread per core) running at 2.3 GHz, 8.0 GB of RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers average CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks but exhibits lower-tier memory bandwidth and general compute scores. Uncached memory read speeds reach 12.56 GB/sec, and write speeds are limited to 6.77 GB/sec. Given these hardware constraints, the a1.xlarge is best utilized for porting software to the arm64 architecture, running lightweight containerized microservices, or managing basic web serving workloads where high-performance memory and advanced instruction sets are not required.
